questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
questions.skill: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread, accounting for outliers
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Salaries at a small company, in thousands of dollars: 40, 42, 45, 45, 48, 50, 250. Find the mean and the median. Which better describes a typical salary?
questions.prompt_markup:
Salaries at a small company, in thousands of dollars: 40, 42, 45, 45, 48, 50, 250.
Find the mean and the median. Which better describes a typical salary?
questions.correct_answer: Mean ≈ 74.29 thousand; median 45 thousand. The median is better: the one salary of 250 pulls the mean up.
questions.grading_note: Form required: both values (the mean to the nearest hundredth or as 520/7) and the choice with a reason.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
questions.skill: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread, accounting for outliers
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: If the salary of 250 is removed, what happens to the mean and to the median?
questions.prompt_markup: If the salary of 250 is removed, what happens to the mean and to the median?
questions.correct_answer: The mean drops from about 74.29 to 45; the median stays 45.
questions.grading_note: Form required: both changes. 270 ÷ 6 = 45, and the middle values are 45 and 45.

sections.skill: Choose measures of center and spread that fit the data

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability
questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread that fit the data
questions.prompt: For data with an extreme outlier, should you report the mean or the median as the center? Why?
questions.prompt_markup: For data with an extreme outlier, should you report the mean or the median as the center? Why?
questions.correct_answer: The median, because one extreme value barely changes it.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the choice and the reason.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability
questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread that fit the data
questions.prompt: For symmetric data with no outliers, which measures of center and spread are usually reported?
questions.prompt_markup: For symmetric data with no outliers, which measures of center and spread are usually reported?
questions.correct_answer: The mean and the mean absolute deviation
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent form. (The mean and the standard deviation are also accepted.)

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability
questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread that fit the data
questions.prompt: Home prices in a town include one mansion. Which measure best describes a typical price?
questions.prompt_markup:
Home prices in a town include one mansion.
Which measure best describes a typical price?
questions.grading_note: The mansion pulls the mean up.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability
questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread that fit the data

questions.prompt_markup: The median is not changed much by a single extreme value.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability
questions.skill: Choose measures of center and spread that fit the data

questions.prompt_markup: The IQR changes greatly when the largest value is made even larger.
questions.grading_note: The IQR depends on Q1 and Q3, which do not change.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a population and a sample?
